title: He Was Not Ready to Love Her… But God Was Already Rewriting Him
paragraphs:
He Was Not Ready to Love Her… But God Was Already Rewriting Him
Becoming the Husband God Is Shaping — When Your Weakness Meets His Cross
He thought being a husband meant providing, protecting, performing.
No one told him it would mean dying.
Not physically… but deeper than that.

Dying to pride.
Dying to silence.
Dying to the version of himself that refused to be healed.
Because somewhere between the wedding vows and the quiet arguments… he realized something terrifying—
He didn’t know how to love her the way she deserved.

And if he’s honest…
he didn’t even know how to love the way God commanded.
The Scripture didn’t whisper about this. It declared it.
In Ephesians 5:25, the Greek doesn’t soften the weight:

“οἱ ἄνδρες, ἀγαπᾶτε τὰς γυναῖκας” (hoi andres, agapate tas gynaikas)
“Husbands, love your wives…”
But not the kind of love the world celebrates.
It continues:

“καθὼς καὶ ὁ Χριστὸς ἠγάπησεν τὴν ἐκκλησίαν”
“just as Christ loved the church…”
And then it pierces deeper—

“καὶ ἑαυτὸν παρέδωκεν ὑπὲρ αὐτῆς”
“and gave Himself up for her.”
Gave Himself.

Not part of Himself.
Not the comfortable parts.
Not the version that looks good in public.
Everything.
This is where most men quietly break.
Because becoming the husband God is shaping isn’t about dominance… it’s about surrender.
And surrender feels like losing—until you realize it’s the only way to actually love.

He remembered the night she cried and he shut down.
The moment she reached for connection and he chose distance.
The times he justified his coldness because “he was tired.”
But God wasn’t measuring his intentions.
God was shaping his heart.
And shaping hurts.

Because the truth is…
some men don’t fail in marriage because they don’t care—
They fail because they’ve never allowed God to confront what’s broken inside them.
The Hebrew understanding of love gives us something even more raw.
In Genesis 2:24, it says:

“וְדָבַק בְּאִשְׁתּוֹ” (vedavaq b’ishto)
“And he shall cling to his wife…”
“Davaq” means to cling, to stick, to pursue with intensity.

Not passive presence.
Not emotional absence.
Clinging.
Which means real love is intentional.

It moves.
It reaches.
It refuses to withdraw when things get uncomfortable.

So when he pulls away instead of pressing in…
when he chooses silence instead of vulnerability…
when he avoids instead of leading with love—
He’s not just hurting her.
He’s resisting what God is trying to build in him.
And God will not stop building.
Because this isn’t just about marriage.
It’s about becoming Christ-like.
In Aramaic, the language Jesus spoke, love carried breath… life… sacrifice.
When Jesus restored Peter in John 21, He didn’t ask about success.
He asked:
“Do you love Me?”
Over and over.
Because everything starts there.
A man who doesn’t love Christ deeply will struggle to love his wife faithfully.
And this is where everything shifts.
Because the goal isn’t to become a perfect husband.
The goal is to become a surrendered one.

A man who lets God expose his anger.
Heal his wounds.
Break his pride.
Rebuild his identity.
A man who stops hiding behind strength and starts walking in truth.
That’s where transformation begins.
That’s where marriages change.
That’s where legacy is rewritten.
And maybe that’s why this hit you harder than expected…
Because you know.

You’ve seen the moments.
Felt the distance.
Heard the silence in your own home.
Be honest.
This isn’t about shame.
It’s about awakening.
Because grace doesn’t ignore your failures—
It meets you in them… and refuses to leave you the same.
The cross wasn’t just for your salvation.
It was for your transformation.

So you can love differently.
Lead differently.
Live differently.
And if this spoke to something real in you…
Don’t keep it to yourself.
And if you’re ready to go deeper…
Because becoming the husband God is shaping isn’t about having it all together—
It’s about finally surrendering the parts you’ve been hiding.
And letting Jesus rewrite what you thought could never change.
You don’t become the man she needs… until you become the man who kneels.
